svg.aria-label: Animated walkthrough of GramSathi: the idea, the five MySQL tables, SQL retrieval, then the complaint flow through the Python app, AI service over REST and manual fallback
svg.title: Animated walkthrough of GramSathi: the idea, the five MySQL tables, SQL retrieval, then the complaint flow through the Python app, AI service over REST and manual fallback

g.text: SQL QUERIES FEED EVERY SCREEN: STAFF SEE WHAT IS NEW, CITIZENS SEE WHAT IS HANDLED
GramSathi digitizes rural governance services: services, applications, complaints and
announcements all live on one Python and MySQL platform.
Users, services, applications, complaints and announcements each get a table, so every record
has one clear home and one clear owner.
Plain SQL queries pull exactly the records each screen needs, such as every new complaint,
A resident reports an issue online, one of the village services GramSathi digitizes.
The complaint is written to the database straight away with a status of new, before any AI is
The app posts the complaint text as JSON to an AI service and gets a category back.
Errors are caught and the complaint goes to manual categorization, so the system keeps working
when the AI service is unavailable.
The categorized complaint is written back to MySQL. Whether AI or a person labelled it, nothing
